idiom_name: functools.singledispatch / singledispatchmethod (generic functions with MRO fallback)
implementation_notes: The standard library ships the mechanism: @functools.singledispatch turns a function into a generic function whose default implementation is the decorated function and whose registered implementations are selected by the type of the first argument, falling back through the method resolution order - the same shape as a tag ladder with a base-tag fallback, except that the decision happens when the call is made, not when the module is compiled. @functools.singledispatchmethod extends this to methods, and typing.overload provides type-checker-only call-site selection with no runtime effect at all. What replaces the classic structure: registration replaces the overload set, the MRO replaces tag inheritance, and the dispatch cache replaces the compiler's overload resolution. The classic form (hand-written dispatch dicts) is justified only when the discriminator is not the first argument's class - a value tag, several arguments, or dispatch on a protocol that cannot be registered.
pitfalls: Registering an implementation on an abstract base class switches dispatch to an extended C3 linearization and can raise 'Ambiguous dispatch' at call time rather than at registration, because ABCs are inserted where their functionality is introduced.

Dispatch is on the type of the first argument only, the registry is mutable state, and PEP 443 notes the registry is not thread-safe - registrations performed during concurrent calls can race with the dispatch cache.

Dispatch decisions are cached and invalidated only by register() (or by an ABC registration changing the cache token), so a dynamic registry built at import time must be complete before the first call to avoid stale choices.
sources: PEP 443 - Single-dispatch generic functions (dispatch algorithm, MRO fallback, ABC linearization, thread-safety note), https://peps.python.org/pep-0443/
